questions.question: Which of the following organism circulates water from their surrounding through their body cavities to facilitate the cells to exchange substances?
questions.explanation: Coelenterates (e.g., sponges and cnidarians) use a water canal system for the exchange of substances. Water circulates through their body cavities, facilitating the movement of nutrients, gases, and waste. This system allows efficient diffusion and exchange directly with their cells.

questions.question: Special fluids for circulation, exchange of nutrients and wastes within body are found in
questions.explanation: Simple unicellular organisms (Option A) exchange nutrients and wastes directly with their environment through diffusion. Simple multicellular organisms (Option B) also rely on diffusion for exchange, as they lack a well-developed circulatory system. Complex multicellular organisms (Option C) require special fluids like blood and lymph for circulation, nutrient transport, and waste removal. All living organisms (Option D) is incorrect because simple organisms do not require special circulatory fluids.

questions.question: Body fluid used by most of the higher organisms for {} the purpose of transportation is
questions.explanation: Blood is the primary body fluid used by most higher organisms for transportation. It circulates oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products throughout the body via the circulatory system. Blood consists of plasma (fluid matrix) and formed elements (RBCs, WBCs, and platelets), ensuring efficient transport and homeostasis.

questions.question: Human blood consists of
questions.explanation: Human blood consists of: Fluid matrix (Plasma): The liquid component making up about 55% of blood, containing water, proteins, and dissolved substances. Formed elements: Includes red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets, which play roles in oxygen transport, immunity, and clotting. Plasma: The non-cellular part of blood that carries nutrients, hormones, and waste products. Since all options are components of blood, "All of these" is the correct choice.

questions.question: Normal blood {pH} is
questions.explanation: Normal human blood pH is slightly alkaline, maintained around 7.4 (ranging from 7.35 to 7.45). This balance is crucial for enzymatic functions, oxygen transport, and overall homeostasis. The body regulates pH through buffer systems, respiratory function, and kidney activity.

questions.question: Plasma is a straw coloured, viscous fluid constituting nearly __________of blood.
questions.explanation: Plasma is the straw-colored, viscous fluid that makes up about 55% of blood. It consists of 90-92% water and 6-8% proteins (such as fibrinogen, globulins, and albumins), along with minerals, nutrients, hormones, and waste products. Plasma plays a crucial role in transport, clotting, and immune functions.

questions.question: Amount of water and protein present in blood plasma is
questions.explanation: Blood plasma consists of 90–92% water, which serves as a medium for transporting nutrients, gases, hormones, and waste. The protein content is 6–8%, including essential proteins like fibrinogen (for clotting), globulins (for immunity), and albumins (for osmotic balance). These components help maintain blood homeostasis and circulation.

questions.question: Major proteins present in plasma is/are
questions.explanation: The major proteins present in plasma are: Fibrinogen: Essential for blood clotting (coagulation). Globulin: Plays a key role in the immune system (antibody production). Albumin: Maintains osmotic balance and regulates blood volume. These proteins collectively contribute to blood function, including transport, immunity, and clotting.

questions.question: Consider the following statements I. Fibrinogens are needed for clotting or coagulation of blood II. Albumins are involved in defense mechanisms of the body
options: Statement I is correct but II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but II is correct
Both statements I & II are correct
Both statements I & II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: Fibrinogens are plasma proteins essential for blood clotting (coagulation). They convert into fibrin during clot formation to prevent excessive blood loss. Statement II is incorrect: Albumins are responsible for maintaining osmotic balance in blood, not for defense. Instead, globulins play a role in the body's immune defense.

questions.question: Globulins contained in human blood plasma are primarily involved in
questions.explanation: Globulins are plasma proteins that play a key role in the immune system. They include immunoglobulins (antibodies), which help in defending the body against infections by identifying and neutralizing pathogens such as bacteria and viruses.

questions.question: I. Plasma contains very low amount of minerals like Na+, Ca2+, Mg2+, HCO3-, Cl-II. Glucose, amino acids, lipids etc. are present in the plasma as they are not always in transit in the bodyIII. Factors for clotting of blood are present in plasma in an active formIV. Plasma without the clotting factors is called serum Find the correct one regarding the above statement
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: Plasma contains small amounts of minerals such as Na⁺, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, HCO₃⁻, and Cl⁻, which help in various physiological functions. Statement II is incorrect: Glucose, amino acids, and lipids are always in transit in the plasma, as they are continuously transported to different cells for metabolism and storage. Statement III is incorrect: Clotting factors are present in plasma in an inactive form and are activated only during injury or trauma. Statement IV is correct: Plasma without clotting factors is called serum and is used in diagnostic and medical applications.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a constituent of formed elements?
questions.explanation: Formed elements of blood include erythrocytes (RBCs), leukocytes (WBCs), and platelets (thrombocytes), which make up about 45% of blood. Plasma is the fluid matrix of blood and is not considered a formed element. It consists mainly of water, proteins, nutrients, and waste products, making up about 55% of blood.

questions.question: Most abundant blood cells in the human body are
questions.explanation: Red Blood Cells (RBCs) or Erythrocytes are the most abundant blood cells in the human body. A healthy adult has approximately 5–5.5 million RBCs per mm³ of blood. RBCs are responsible for oxygen transport due to the presence of hemoglobin and have a lifespan of about 120 days.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Average life span of RBCs is 120 days
The number of {RBC} in adult man per cubic {mm} of blood is 5 million to 5.5 million
RBCs are formed in the red bone marrow in adults
RBCs are devoid of nucleus in most of the mammals and are biconvex in shape
questions.explanation: RBCs are actually biconcave in shape, not biconvex. This shape increases the surface area for oxygen exchange and flexibility for movement through capillaries. Other statements are correct: RBC lifespan is around 120 days. RBC count in a healthy adult is 5 to 5.5 million per mm³ of blood. RBCs are formed in the red bone marrow in adults through the process of erythropoiesis.

questions.question: Which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Blood consists of plasma (fluid matrix) and formed elements (RBCs, WBCs, and platelets). Option A is incorrect because lymph lacks RBCs and mainly contains WBCs. Option C is incorrect because plasma is blood without formed elements (RBCs, WBCs, and platelets), not just lymphocytes. Option D is incorrect because serum is plasma without fibrinogen, not blood + fibrinogen.

questions.question: Amount of haemoglobin present in 100 {ml} of blood
questions.explanation: The normal hemoglobin (Hb) level in a healthy adult human ranges from 12 to 16 g per 100 mL of blood. Males generally have 13-16 g/dL, while females have 12-14 g/dL. Hemoglobin is an iron-containing protein in RBCs that plays a crucial role in oxygen transport throughout the body.

questions.question: Which of the following organ is considered as {} graveyard of RBCs?
questions.explanation: The spleen is known as the "graveyard of RBCs" because it is the primary site where old and damaged red blood cells (RBCs) are broken down. It helps in filtering blood, removing aged RBCs, and recycling iron from hemoglobin. Although the liver (option B) also plays a role in RBC breakdown, the spleen is the main organ responsible for this function.

questions.question: Which statement is true for WBCs?
options: Lesser in number and long lived
questions.explanation: White Blood Cells (WBCs) exhibit a property called diapedesis, which allows them to cross the walls of blood capillaries and migrate to sites of infection or injury. Option A is incorrect because WBCs are colorless, as they lack hemoglobin. Option C is incorrect because WBCs are nucleated. Option D is partially correct, but not all WBCs are long-lived; some, like neutrophils, have a short lifespan, while lymphocytes can survive longer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an agranulocyte?
questions.explanation: White Blood Cells (WBCs) are classified into granulocytes (having granules in the cytoplasm) and agranulocytes (lacking granules). Lymphocytes are agranulocytes and play a crucial role in the immune response, including antibody production and cell-mediated immunity. Basophils, Neutrophils, and Eosinophils are granulocytes, as they contain visible cytoplasmic granules.

questions.question: The correct descending order of the percentage proportion of leucocytes in human blood is:
questions.explanation: The correct descending order of leukocytes (WBCs) in human blood based on their percentage is: Neutrophils (60–65%) → First line of defense, phagocytic. Lymphocytes (20–25%) → Responsible for immune response (B and T cells). Monocytes (6–8%) → Phagocytic cells, transform into macrophages. Eosinophils (2–3%) → Involved in allergic reactions and parasitic infections. Basophils (0.5–1%) → Least abundant, release histamine in allergic responses.

questions.question: The most active phagocytic white blood cells are
questions.explanation: Neutrophils are the most abundant phagocytic white blood cells and act as the first line of defense against infections. They engulf and destroy pathogens. Monocytes are also highly phagocytic and transform into macrophages, which are long-lived phagocytes that help in removing pathogens and dead cells. Other options are incorrect because: Eosinophils (in A & C) are mainly involved in allergic reactions and parasitic infections, not primary phagocytosis. Lymphocytes (in A & D) are responsible for adaptive immunity rather than phagocytosis.

questions.question: Plasma is a straw coloured viscous fluid constituting nearly ____A_ % of the blood,__ B_% of the plasma is water; and the protein constitutes _____C ____% of it Choose the correct option for the blanks A, B and C.
questions.explanation: Plasma constitutes about 55% of total blood volume (A = 55%). Plasma is primarily water (90-92%) (B = 90-92%), which helps in transport and maintaining blood fluidity. Proteins (Albumin, Globulin, and Fibrinogen) make up 6-8% of plasma (C = 6-8%) and are essential for functions like clotting, immunity, and osmotic balance.

questions.question: A healthy individual has ____A__ grams of haemoglobin in every ___B____ {mL} of blood. These molecules play a significant role in the transport of___C_____ gases Choose the correct option for A, B and C
questions.explanation: A (Hemoglobin levels): A healthy individual has 12-16 grams of hemoglobin per 100 mL of blood. Men: 13-18 g/100 mL Women: 12-16 g/100 mL B (Blood volume reference): Hemoglobin concentration is measured per 100 mL of blood. C (Function): Hemoglobin is responsible for transporting respiratory gases (oxygen and carbon dioxide) in the blood. Why other options are incorrect: B (6-8 g/100 mL): Too low, indicative of anemia. C & D (B-1000 mL): Hemoglobin levels are measured per 100 mL, not 1000 mL. D (16-20 g/100 mL): Higher than the normal range.

questions.question: Which proteins are involved in defense mechanisms of the body?
questions.explanation: Globulins are a class of plasma proteins that play a major role in the immune defense mechanism. Immunoglobulins (antibodies), a type of globulin, help in fighting infections by recognizing and neutralizing pathogens (bacteria, viruses, etc.). Why other options are incorrect: B (Albumin): Maintains osmotic balance and transports substances but does not play a direct role in immunity. C (Fibrinogen): Involved in blood clotting, not immune defense. D (None of the above): Incorrect, as globulins are directly involved in the body's defense mechanisms.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is incorrect?
options: The RBCs of camel are oval and nucleated
Blood clotting factors are present in plasma
Human RBCs lack nuclei but have mitochondria
In adults, erythropoiesis occurs in the bone marrow
questions.explanation: Human RBCs lack both a nucleus and mitochondria to make space for hemoglobin, which enhances their oxygen-carrying capacity. Without mitochondria, RBCs rely on anaerobic glycolysis for energy production. Why other statements are correct: A (✔) The RBCs of camels are oval and nucleated – Unlike most mammals, camel RBCs are oval and retain their nucleus, which helps them survive dehydration. B (✔) Blood clotting factors are present in plasma – Fibrinogen, prothrombin, and other clotting factors are found in plasma and aid in blood coagulation. D (✔) In adults, erythropoiesis occurs in the bone marrow – Red bone marrow is the site of RBC production in adults, stimulated by erythropoietin (EPO) from the kidneys. Thus, the incorrect statement is C, making it the correct answer for this question.

questions.question: Blood grouping which is/are widely used all over the world are
questions.explanation: The ABO blood grouping system and the Rh (Rhesus) factor are the two major blood group classification systems used worldwide. ABO Grouping (A) – Based on the presence or absence of A and B antigens on the surface of RBCs, leading to four blood groups: A, B, AB, and O Rh Grouping (B) – Determines whether the Rh antigen (D antigen) is present (+) or absent (-). Rh-positive (Rh⁺) means the Rh antigen is present. Rh-negative (Rh⁻) means the Rh antigen is absent. Both systems are crucial in blood transfusions and organ transplants to prevent immune reactions. Why other options are incorrect: A (Only ABO grouping): Incomplete, as Rh grouping is also widely used. B (Only Rh grouping): Incomplete, as ABO grouping is the primary system. D (None of the above): Incorrect, as both ABO and Rh systems are globally recognized.

questions.question: Person with blood group {AB} is considered as universal recipient because he/she has:
options: both {A} and {B} antigens on RBCs but no antibodies in the plasma.
both A and B antibodies in the plasma.
no antigen on RBCs and no antibody in the plasma.
both {A} and {B} antigens in the plasma but no antibodies.
questions.explanation: A person with blood group AB is considered the universal recipient because: Their RBCs have both A and B antigens. Their plasma lacks anti-A and anti-B antibodies, meaning they can receive blood from any ABO group without an immune reaction. Why other options are incorrect: B (Both A and B antibodies in the plasma): Incorrect, as AB blood group does not have any antibodies. C (No antigen on RBCs and no antibody in the plasma): Incorrect, as AB blood group has both A and B antigens on RBCs. D (Both A and B antigens in the plasma but no antibodies): Incorrect, as antigens are on RBCs, not in plasma.

questions.question: A certain road accident patient with unknown blood group needs immediate blood transfusion. His one doctor friend at once offers his blood. What was the blood group of the donor?
questions.explanation: Blood group O is the universal donor because: It lacks A and B antigens on RBCs, so it does not cause an immune reaction in recipients of any blood group. It can be safely transfused to patients of any blood group (A, B, AB, or O) in emergencies when the recipient’s blood group is unknown. In emergency situations, O-negative blood is preferred since it also lacks the Rh factor, reducing the risk of reaction.

questions.question: Which one of the following plasma protein is involved in the coagulation of blood?
questions.explanation: Fibrinogen is a plasma protein essential for blood clotting (coagulation). During coagulation, fibrinogen is converted into fibrin by thrombin, forming a mesh-like clot that prevents excessive bleeding. It is produced in the liver and is one of the key clotting factors. Why other options are incorrect: A (Albumin): Maintains osmotic balance and transports substances but does not play a role in clotting. B (Serum amylase): A digestive enzyme that breaks down starch, unrelated to blood coagulation. C (Globulin): Involved in immune responses (immunoglobulins), not blood clotting.

questions.question: A child of O-group has B-group father. The genotype of father will be
questions.explanation: Blood group O child means the child has genotype IᴼIᴼ (homozygous recessive). The child inherits one Iᴼ allele from each parent. The father has B blood group, meaning his genotype can be either IᴮIᴮ or IᴮIᴼ. To pass an Iᴼ allele to the child, the father must have the genotype IᴮIᴼ (heterozygous for B). Why other options are incorrect: A (IᴼIᴼ): This genotype belongs to someone with O blood group, not B. B (IᴮIᴮ): This would mean the father only carries B alleles and cannot pass an Iᴼ allele to the child. C (IᴬIᴮ): This genotype corresponds to AB blood group, not B.

questions.question: A person with blood group A requires blood. The blood group which can be given is
questions.explanation: A person with blood group A has A antigens on RBCs and anti-B antibodies in plasma. This means they cannot receive blood from blood group B or AB, as these contain B antigens, which would cause an immune reaction. They can safely receive blood from: A group (same antigen, no reaction) O group (universal donor, no antigens present to trigger a reaction) Why other options are incorrect: A (A & B): Incorrect, as B blood group would cause an immune reaction. B (A & AB): Incorrect, as AB blood contains B antigens, which would be rejected. D (A, B, AB & O): Incorrect, as B and AB blood are incompatible.

questions.question: What type of cells are involved in inflammatory and allergic reactions?
questions.explanation: Mast cells play a key role in inflammatory and allergic reactions by releasing histamine and other inflammatory mediators. These cells are found in connective tissues and are activated in response to allergens, leading to vasodilation, increased permeability, and recruitment of immune cells. Why other options are incorrect: A (Neutrophils): Involved in bacterial infections and acute inflammation, but not directly in allergic reactions. B (Monocytes): Differentiate into macrophages and participate in chronic inflammation, not acute allergic responses. C (Dendritic cells): Antigen-presenting cells that activate adaptive immunity, but they are not primary mediators of allergic reactions.

questions.question: Factors present on surface of RBCs related to heredity are:
questions.explanation: Antigens on the surface of RBCs are inherited and determine a person's blood group (ABO and Rh systems). These antigens are glycoproteins or glycolipids and are genetically inherited from parents. ABO blood group system is determined by the presence of A and B antigens on RBCs. Rh factor (D antigen) is another inherited antigen that classifies blood as Rh-positive or Rh-negative.

questions.question: Blood group is due to:
options: specific antigens on the surface of WBCs.
specific antibodies on the surface of RBCs.
specific antigens on the surface of RBCs.
questions.explanation: Blood groups are determined by the presence of specific antigens on the surface of RBCs. The ABO blood group system is based on the presence or absence of A and B antigens on RBCs. The Rh factor (D antigen) determines whether a person is Rh-positive or Rh-negative. These antigens are genetically inherited and play a crucial role in blood transfusions and organ compatibility. Why other options are incorrect: A (Specific antigens on the surface of WBCs): Incorrect, as blood groups are related to RBC surface antigens, not WBCs. B (Specific antibodies on the surface of RBCs): Incorrect, as antibodies are present in plasma, not on RBCs. D (Type of haemoglobin): Incorrect, as haemoglobin is responsible for oxygen transport, not blood grouping.

questions.question: For safe blood transfusion:
options: donor's RBC should not contain antibodies against recipient's serum.
recipient's serum should not contain antigens against donor's antibodies.
recipient's serum should not contain antibodies against RBCs of donors.
recipient's RBCs should not contain antibodies against donor's antigens.
questions.explanation: For a safe blood transfusion, the recipient’s serum must not contain antibodies that react with the donor's RBC antigens. If the recipient has antibodies against the donor's RBCs, an immune reaction (hemolysis or agglutination) occurs, leading to serious transfusion reactions. For example, a Type A recipient has anti-B antibodies, so they cannot receive blood from Type B or AB donors, as their antibodies will attack the B antigen on donor RBCs. Why other options are incorrect: A (Donor’s RBC should not contain antibodies against recipient’s serum): Incorrect, because RBCs do not contain antibodies—they have antigens. B (Recipient’s serum should not contain antigens against donor’s antibodies): Incorrect, as antigens are on RBCs, not in serum. D (Recipient’s RBCs should not contain antibodies against donor’s antigens): Incorrect, as RBCs do not contain antibodies—only plasma does.

questions.question: Lymph serves to
options: Return the interstitial fluid to the blood
Return the WBCs and RBCs to the lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Lymph is a clear fluid derived from interstitial fluid, which is collected by lymphatic capillaries and returned to the circulatory system. It plays a vital role in maintaining fluid balance by draining excess fluid from tissues back into the bloodstream via the subclavian veins. It also helps in immune responses by transporting WBCs (especially lymphocytes) and filtering pathogens in lymph nodes. Why other options are incorrect: B (Return WBCs and RBCs to the lymph nodes): Lymph transports WBCs, but not RBCs, which are confined to blood circulation. C (Transport CO₂ to the lungs): CO₂ is carried by blood, not lymph, primarily as bicarbonate ions (HCO₃⁻). D (Transport O₂ to the brain): O₂ transport is a function of hemoglobin in blood, not lymph.

questions.question: A dark reddish brown scum formed at the site of cut or an injury over a period of time which is called
questions.explanation: When an injury occurs, blood clotting (coagulation) prevents excessive bleeding. The dark reddish-brown scum formed at the site of injury consists of a clot (coagulum) made up of a network of fibrin fibers, RBCs, platelets, and other cells. Fibrin, a protein formed from fibrinogen during clotting, helps trap blood components to seal the wound. Why other options are incorrect: A (Clot): Correct but incomplete; the correct term is coagulum. B (Scar): Incorrect, as a scar is a fibrous tissue formed after healing, not the initial clot. C (Coagulum): Correct but incomplete; clot and coagulum are synonymous in this context.

questions.question: Identify {A} and {B} Prothrombin {A}{} Thrombin Fibrinogen {{B}}{} Fibrin
questions.explanation: Prothrombin → Thrombin Prothrombin is an inactive plasma protein that is converted into thrombin by the action of thrombokinase (also called prothrombinase) in the presence of Ca²⁺ ions. Fibrinogen → Fibrin Fibrinogen is a soluble plasma protein that is converted into insoluble fibrin by the action of thrombin. Fibrin forms a mesh that traps RBCs and platelets, leading to clot formation.

questions.question: During blood coagulation, vitamin {K} helps in
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of prothrombin, a crucial clotting factor produced in the liver. It also assists in the formation of other clotting factors such as Factors VII, IX, and X, which are necessary for effective blood coagulation. Without sufficient vitamin K, prothrombin levels decrease, leading to prolonged clotting time and excessive bleeding. Why other options are incorrect: B (Formation of thromboplastin): Thromboplastin is released from damaged tissues and platelets, not directly formed by vitamin K. C (Conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin): This step is carried out by thrombin, not vitamin K. D (Conversion of prothrombin to thrombin): This process is catalyzed by thrombokinase and calcium ions, not vitamin K.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is incorrect?
options: A person of {O} blood group has anti {A} and anti B antibodies in his blood plasma
A person of {B} blood group can not donate blood to a person of A blood group
Blood group is designated on the basis of the presence of antibodies in the blood plasma
A person of {AB} blood group is universal recipient
questions.explanation: Blood grouping is determined by the presence of specific antigens on the surface of RBCs, not by antibodies in plasma. The ABO blood group system is based on the presence or absence of A and B antigens on RBCs: Type A: Has A antigen, with anti-B antibodies in plasma. Type B: Has B antigen, with anti-A antibodies in plasma. Type AB: Has both A and B antigens, with no antibodies (universal recipient). Type O: Has no A or B antigens, but has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies (universal donor).

questions.question: Which of the following anticoagulant is secreted by leech?
questions.explanation: Hirudin is a potent anticoagulant secreted by leeches (Hirudo medicinalis) to prevent blood clotting while they feed on their host's blood. It works by directly inhibiting thrombin, preventing the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin, which is essential for blood clotting. It is often used in medical applications for its anticoagulant properties. Why other options are incorrect: A. Heparin: A natural anticoagulant but produced by mast cells and basophils in mammals, not by leeches. C. Serotonin: A neurotransmitter involved in mood regulation, also plays a role in vasoconstriction but not as an anticoagulant. D. Histamine: Involved in allergic reactions and vasodilation, but does not prevent blood clotting. Thus, the correct answer is Hirudin, which is secreted by leeches to keep the blood from clotting while they feed.

questions.question: Thrombokinase is associated with
options: Production of erythrocytes from the bone marrow
Enzymatic reactions in coagulation of blood
questions.explanation: Thrombokinase (also known as thrombokinase or prothrombinase) is an enzyme that plays a crucial role in blood coagulation (clotting). It catalyzes the conversion of prothrombin into thrombin, which then helps in the formation of a fibrin clot. This process is essential for stopping bleeding and initiating wound healing. Why other options are incorrect: A. Production of erythrocytes from the bone marrow → This is the process of erythropoiesis, regulated by the hormone erythropoietin, not thrombokinase. B. Pulmonary and systemic circulation → This involves the movement of blood between the heart, lungs, and body but is unrelated to thrombokinase. C. Cardiac cycle and its regulation → The cardiac cycle is controlled by electrical impulses (SA node, AV node) and hormonal regulation, not thrombokinase.

questions.question: Read the statements given below and choose the correct sequence of events leading the formation of a blood clot (i) Calcium activates an enzyme (ii) Fibrin binds platelets to form a ‘plug’ (iii) Thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin (iv) Platelets and damaged cells release an activator
Which of the following conditions cause erythroblastosis foetalis?
questions.explanation: Erythroblastosis fetalis (Hemolytic Disease of the Newborn) occurs when: The mother is Rh-negative (Rh⁻). The fetus is Rh-positive (Rh⁺) (inherited from an Rh⁺ father). During childbirth or pregnancy complications, fetal Rh⁺ RBCs enter the mother's bloodstream. The mother's immune system produces antibodies against Rh⁺ RBCs. If the mother becomes pregnant again with an Rh⁺ fetus, the antibodies cross the placenta and attack fetal RBCs, leading to severe hemolysis, anemia, jaundice, and potential fetal death.

questions.question: Clot is formed mainly of a network of threads called:
questions.explanation: Blood clot formation is a complex process called coagulation. It primarily involves the conversion of fibrinogen (a soluble plasma protein) into fibrin (an insoluble thread-like protein), which forms the meshwork of the clot. Prothrombin (inactive form) is converted into thrombin (active enzyme). Thrombin catalyzes the conversion of fibrinogen into fibrin. Fibrin forms a network of insoluble protein threads that trap blood cells and platelets, creating a stable clot.

questions.question: If husband has blood group {O} and wife blood group A B , the blood group of the child cannot be
questions.explanation: Blood group inheritance follows Mendelian genetics, specifically codominance for the ABO system. Each parent contributes one allele to the child. Blood group O means the husband has genotype ii (homozygous recessive for O). Blood group AB means the wife has genotype IAIB. Possible Blood Groups for the Child: Each child inherits one allele from each parent: From the husband: Only i (O) is possible. From the wife: Can pass IA (A) or IB (B). Thus, the child’s possible blood groups are: IAi (A) IBi (B) Blood Groups the Child CANNOT Have: Blood group O (ii) → Requires both parents to contribute i, but the mother does not have an i allele. Blood group AB (IAIB) → Requires the child to inherit IA from one parent and IB from the other, which is impossible since the father only has i.

questions.question: Which one of the following substances, if introduced in blood stream would cause coagulation of blood at the site of its introduction?
questions.explanation: Thromboplastin plays a crucial role in the coagulation cascade by initiating the conversion of prothrombin into thrombin, which in turn converts fibrinogen into fibrin, leading to clot formation. Roles of the given substances: Prothrombin (A): A precursor protein that needs to be activated by thromboplastin and calcium to form thrombin. Fibrinogen (B): A plasma protein that gets converted into fibrin only in the presence of thrombin. Thromboplastin (C): Directly triggers the coagulation process by initiating the extrinsic pathway. Heparin (D): An anticoagulant, which prevents clotting rather than inducing it.

questions.question: Chances of erythroblastosis foetalis occurring during second pregnancy when the baby is:
questions.explanation: Erythroblastosis fetalis, also known as hemolytic disease of the newborn (HDN), occurs when there is an incompatibility between the Rh factor of the mother and the fetus. If a Rh-negative mother (Rh-ve) carries a Rh-positive baby (Rh+ve), during the first pregnancy, the mother may be exposed to Rh+ve blood from the fetus. This leads to the production of anti-Rh antibodies in the mother. In subsequent pregnancies, if the next baby is Rh-positive, the mother's antibodies can attack the fetal Rh-positive red blood cells, leading to erythroblastosis fetalis. This condition does not occur if: The mother and baby both have Rh-negative (Rh-ve) or both are Rh-positive (Rh+ve) because there is no antigen-antibody reaction. It is also less common if the baby is Rh-negative and the mother is Rh-positive, because there is no risk of antibody formation in such cases.

questions.question: Which of the following cations is required for the conversion of prothrombin into active thrombin by thromboplastin?
questions.explanation: During blood clotting, calcium ions (Ca²⁺) are essential for the activation of prothrombin into thrombin. This process occurs through the action of thromboplastin, which requires calcium ions to catalyze the conversion of prothrombin into thrombin, which then helps in the formation of fibrin threads to form the clot. Calcium ions play a crucial role in the coagulation cascade. Thus, Ca²⁺ is the required cation in this process.

questions.question: Blood clotting requires
questions.explanation: Blood clotting requires calcium ions (Ca²⁺) and thromboplastin (also known as tissue factor). Calcium ions are crucial for several steps in the clotting cascade, including the conversion of prothrombin into thrombin, which is essential for blood clot formation. Thromboplastin also activates this pathway during injury or damage to blood vessels.

questions.question: Blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities called:
questions.explanation: In open circulatory systems, blood (or hemolymph) is pumped by the heart into large open spaces or body cavities called sinuses instead of enclosed blood vessels. This allows direct exchange of nutrients and gases between the hemolymph and body cells. Artery (A) → Incorrect, because arteries are blood vessels that carry oxygenated blood away from the heart in a closed circulatory system. Lymph node (B) → Incorrect, as lymph nodes are not involved in direct circulation of blood; they are immune structures that filter lymph. Vein (C) → Incorrect, because veins return blood to the heart but do not open into body cavities. Sinuses (D) → Correct, because in open circulation (e.g., in arthropods and mollusks), the blood is released into sinuses, allowing it to flow freely before being recollected into the heart. [NCERT (2025-26) Class 11th Page no. 000]

questions.question: Circulatory system is absent in
questions.explanation: Flatworms (Platyhelminthes) lack a circulatory system. Instead, they rely on diffusion for the transport of gases and nutrients due to their thin, flattened bodies, which allow direct exchange with the environment. Annelida, Arthropoda, and Cephalopoda possess circulatory systems, with Annelida having a closed circulatory system, Arthropoda having an open circulatory system, and Cephalopoda having a well-developed closed circulatory system.

questions.question: The circulatory pattern in which blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities is
questions.explanation: In an open circulatory system, the blood (hemolymph) is pumped by the heart into large vessels that open into body cavities called sinuses, where it directly bathes the organs. This system is found in arthropods and most mollusks. Unlike the closed circulatory system, where blood remains confined within vessels, the open system allows direct exchange of substances between hemolymph and tissues.

questions.question: Which ones have open circulatory system? A. Ascidia B. Cockroach C. Earthworm D. Prawn E. Silver Fish F. Snail
questions.explanation: Organisms with an open circulatory system include: Cockroach (B) – Arthropods have an open circulatory system where hemolymph flows into body cavities (sinuses). Prawn (D) – A crustacean (arthropod) with an open circulatory system. Silverfish (E) – An insect (arthropod) with an open circulatory system. Snail (F) – A mollusc with an open circulatory system, except for cephalopods, which have a closed system. Earthworm (C) has a closed circulatory system, and Ascidia (A), a tunicate, has a partially closed system.

questions.question: Closed circulatory system is present in A. Arthropoda B. Annelida C. Chordata D. Mollusca
questions.explanation: A closed circulatory system is present in: Annelida (B) – Earthworms and other annelids have a well-developed closed circulatory system where blood flows within vessels. Chordata (C) – Vertebrates (fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals) have a closed circulatory system, ensuring efficient transport of oxygen and nutrients.

questions.question: The blood vascular system in hemichordata is
Single heart circuit occurs in
questions.explanation: Fishes exhibit single circulation, where the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills for oxygenation, and the oxygenated blood is then supplied to the body before returning to the heart. In contrast, frogs (B), reptiles (C), and humans (D) have some form of double circulation, ensuring better separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

questions.question: How many chambers are found in avian heart?
questions.explanation: Birds (Aves) have a four-chambered heart consisting of two atria and two ventricles. This ensures complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, allowing efficient circulation to support their high metabolic rate required for flight.

questions.question: In crocodiles, heart is
questions.explanation: Crocodiles have a four-chambered heart, which is unique among reptiles. Unlike other reptiles with a three-chambered heart, crocodiles have two atria and two ventricles, ensuring complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood. However, they possess a special adaptation allowing some mixing of blood when diving.

questions.question: 2 and 4 chambered hearts are found in
questions.explanation: Fishes have a two-chambered heart (one atrium and one ventricle) with single circulation, meaning blood passes through the heart only once per cycle. Crocodiles have a four-chambered heart (two atria and two ventricles), which fully separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, similar to birds and mammals. Other reptiles (except crocodiles) have a three-chambered heart.

questions.question: Circulation in human is:
questions.explanation: Humans have a double circulation system, meaning blood passes through the heart twice in one complete cycle: Pulmonary circulation – Blood moves from the heart to the lungs for oxygenation and back. Systemic circulation – Oxygenated blood is pumped from the heart to the body and returns as deoxygenated blood. Additionally, humans have a closed circulatory system, where blood flows entirely within blood vessels, ensuring efficient transport of oxygen and nutrients.

questions.question: Which one of the following animal has two separate circulatory pathways?
questions.explanation: Whales, being mammals, have a double circulatory system, meaning they have two separate circulatory pathways: Pulmonary circulation – Carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs for oxygenation and back. Systemic circulation – Distributes oxygenated blood from the heart to the body and returns deoxygenated blood. Other options: Lizards (A) and Frogs (D) have a three-chambered heart with incomplete double circulation due to partial mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood. Sharks (C) have a single circulation system with a two-chambered heart where blood passes through the heart only once per cycle.

questions.question: Which animal has most mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in the ventricles?
questions.explanation: Frogs have a three-chambered heart consisting of two atria and one ventricle. Since the ventricle is undivided, there is significant mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, leading to incomplete double circulation. Other options: Scoliodon (A) (Shark) has a two-chambered heart with single circulation, meaning no mixing occurs in the ventricles. Rabbit (B) is a mammal with a four-chambered heart, ensuring complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

questions.question: Match the columns I and II, and choose the correct combination from the options given
questions.explanation: Matching the circulatory systems: Fishes (A-1) → Single circulation (Blood passes through the heart once per cycle). Amphibians (B-2) → Incomplete double circulation (Three-chambered heart, partial mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood). Reptiles (C-2) → Incomplete double circulation (Except crocodiles, most reptiles have a three-chambered heart). Birds (D-3) → Double circulation (Four-chambered heart, complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood). Mammals (E-3) → Double circulation (Four-chambered heart with complete separation).

questions.question: Human heart is enclosed in a double walled sac called as
questions.explanation: The human heart is enclosed in a double-walled sac called the pericardium, which contains pericardial fluid. This fluid reduces friction between the heart and surrounding structures during contractions. Other options: Peritoneum (A) – Lines the abdominal cavity. Pericardial sinus (C) – Found in open circulatory systems of arthropods. Perineural sinus (D) – Part of the circulatory system in arthropods.

questions.question: Tricuspid valve is found in between
questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve is located between the right atrium (auricle) and the right ventricle. It prevents backflow of blood from the right ventricle into the right atrium during ventricular contraction. It consists of three cusps and ensures unidirectional blood flow toward the pulmonary circulation.

questions.question: Mitral valve in mammals guards the opening between:
questions.explanation: The mitral valve (also called the bicuspid valve) is located between the left atrium (auricle) and the left ventricle in mammals. It prevents the backflow of oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the left atrium during ventricular contraction, ensuring unidirectional blood flow into the aorta.

questions.question: The right and left ventricles open into:
options: The pulmonary artery and the aorta
questions.explanation: The right ventricle opens into the pulmonary artery, which carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation. The left ventricle opens into the aorta, which carries oxygenated blood to the entire body. These openings are guarded by semilunar valves, which prevent backflow of blood into the ventricles.

questions.question: To reach the left side of the heart, the blood must pass through
questions.explanation: To reach the left side of the heart, blood must first pass through the lungs for oxygenation. Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium, then moves to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. In the lungs, blood gets oxygenated and then returns to the left atrium via the pulmonary veins before being pumped to the body by the left ventricle. Other options: Sinus venosus (A) is present in fish and amphibians but not in adult humans. Kidneys (B) and Liver (C) filter blood but do not directly send it to the left side of the heart.

questions.question: In amphibians and reptiles, ....A..... atrium receives oxygenated blood from the gills/lung/skin and ......B....atrium gets the .....C..... blood from other body parts Choose the correct option for A, B and C
questions.explanation: In amphibians and reptiles, the left atrium (A-left) receives oxygenated blood from the lungs, gills, or skin. The right atrium (B-right) receives deoxygenated blood (C-deoxygenated) from the rest of the body. These organisms generally have a three-chambered heart (except crocodiles, which have four chambers), where some mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood occurs in the ventricle.

questions.question: When the right ventricle contracts, the blood is pump into
questions.explanation: When the right ventricle contracts, it pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery (also called the pulmonary aorta), which carries the blood to the lungs for oxygenation. Other options: Superior vena cava (A) brings deoxygenated blood into the right atrium, not out of the ventricle. Dorsal aorta (B) is part of the systemic circulation and carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body. Pulmonary veins (D) carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

questions.question: The wall of human heart is thick due to presence of
questions.explanation: The thickness of the human heart wall is primarily due to the myocardium, which is the middle muscular layer of the heart. The myocardium is composed of cardiac muscle fibers responsible for the contraction and pumping action of the heart. Other options: Endocardium (A) → The inner layer that lines the heart chambers. Pericardium (C) → The outermost protective sac that encloses the heart. Epicardium (D) → The outer layer of the heart wall, part of the pericardium, but not responsible for thickness.

questions.question: The Pulmonary artery arise from
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery arises from the right ventricle and carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation. This is unique because it is the only artery that carries deoxygenated blood. Other options: Left ventricle (A) → Gives rise to the aorta, which carries oxygenated blood to the body. Left auricle (C) and Right auricle (D) → These are atria that receive blood but do not give rise to major arteries.

questions.question: Chordae tendinae are found in
questions.explanation: Chordae tendineae are tendon-like structures found in the ventricles of the heart. They are attached to the cusps of the atrioventricular (AV) valves (tricuspid and bicuspid/mitral valves) and connect to the papillary muscles in the ventricles. Their function is to prevent valve prolapse and backflow of blood during ventricular contraction.

questions.question: Which one of the following has the thickest walls?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle has the thickest walls because it pumps oxygenated blood to the entire body through the aorta. This requires a much higher pressure compared to the right ventricle, which only pumps blood to the lungs. Other options: Right auricle (A) and Left auricle (B) → Have thin walls as they only receive blood and do not pump it with force. Right ventricle (C) → Has thinner walls than the left ventricle since it pumps blood only to the lungs, which require lower pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following has a closed type of circulatory system?
questions.explanation: A closed circulatory system means that blood flows entirely within vessels and does not directly bathe the organs. Fish have a closed circulatory system with a two-chambered heart, where blood is pumped through a network of blood vessels. Cockroach (A) and Scorpion (D) are arthropods and have an open circulatory system, where blood (hemolymph) is pumped into open sinuses. Mollusca (C) mostly have an open circulatory system, except cephalopods (e.g., octopuses and squids), which have a closed system.

questions.question: Pacemaker is situated in heart
options: In the wall of right atrium
In the wall of left atrium
questions.explanation: The pacemaker of the heart, also known as the sinoatrial (SA) node, is located in the wall of the right atrium near the opening of the superior vena cava. The SA node generates electrical impulses that initiate and regulate the heart's rhythmic contractions, making it the natural pacemaker of the heart.

questions.question: Sino-atrial node (SAN) is a patch of nodal tissue present in
options: Right upper corner of right atrium
Left upper corner of right atrium
Right lower corner of left atrium
Left lower corner of left atrium
questions.explanation: The sinoatrial node (SA node) is a patch of nodal tissue located in the right upper corner of the right atrium, near the opening of the superior vena cava. It functions as the natural pacemaker of the heart, initiating and regulating the heart's rhythmic contractions by generating electrical impulses.

questions.question: Human heart has SA node which makes it:
questions.explanation: The human heart is myogenic, meaning it generates its own rhythmic contractions due to the sinoatrial (SA) node, which acts as the natural pacemaker. This allows the heart to beat autonomously without requiring direct nervous system stimulation. Neurogenic heart (B) is found in some invertebrates like arthropods, where nerve impulses control heartbeats. Digenic heart (C) and Rhinogenic heart (D) are not valid biological terms.

questions.question: In bird and mammals, the oxygenated blood is received by .......A....... and deoxygenated blood is received by .....B...... .The ventricles pump it out without any mixing up of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood. Choose the correct option for A and B
questions.explanation: In birds and mammals, the heart is four-chambered, ensuring complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood: The left atrium (A-left atria) receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins. The right atrium (B-right atria) receives deoxygenated blood from the body via the vena cava. The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the body through the aorta, and the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. This double circulation system allows efficient oxygen delivery without mixing oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

questions.question: Tricupsid valve is found in between
questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve is located between the right atrium and the right ventricle. It prevents backflow of blood into the right atrium when the right ventricle contracts, ensuring unidirectional blood flow toward the pulmonary circulation. Other options: Sinus venosus and right atrium (A) → Sinus venosus is present in lower vertebrates like fish and amphibians, not in mammals. Left ventricle and left atrium (C) → This is guarded by the bicuspid (mitral) valve, not the tricuspid valve. Ventricle and aorta (D) → This is controlled by the aortic semilunar valve, not the tricuspid valve.

questions.question: Heart of fishes is
questions.explanation: Fishes have a two-chambered heart (A) consisting of one atrium and one ventricle. It is also called a venous heart (B) because it receives only deoxygenated blood and pumps it to the gills for oxygenation (single circulation). Thus, both statements (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.question: Open type of vascular system is predominant in
questions.explanation: An open circulatory system is found in arthropods, where blood (hemolymph) is pumped into open spaces or sinuses rather than confined to blood vessels. This system is less efficient than a closed circulatory system. Other options: Fishes (A) → Have a closed circulatory system with a two-chambered heart. Amphibians (C) → Have a closed circulatory system with a three-chambered heart. Earthworms (D) → Belong to Annelida and possess a closed circulatory system.

questions.question: All reptiles have a three-chambered heart except
questions.explanation: Most reptiles have a three-chambered heart (two atria and one ventricle), where partial mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood occurs. However, crocodiles are an exception, as they have a four-chambered heart with complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, similar to birds and mammals. Snake (A) and Lizard (C) have a three-chambered heart. Crocodiles (B) possess a four-chambered heart, making them the exception.

questions.question: Three chambered heart is found in
questions.explanation: Frogs, like other amphibians, have a three-chambered heart, which consists of: Two atria (left and right) One ventricle (where partial mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood occurs) This allows for incomplete double circulation. Other options: Fish (A) → Have a two-chambered heart (one atrium, one ventricle). Rabbit (C) and Man (D) → Both are mammals with a four-chambered heart (two atria, two ventricles) ensuring complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

questions.question: Ventricle is thick walled as compared to auricle because
options: It is present on the posterior side
It is to pump blood with more force
It is to receive blood from auricles
questions.explanation: The ventricles have thicker walls than the atria (auricles) because they need to pump blood with greater force. The left ventricle has the thickest wall as it pumps oxygenated blood to the entire body through the aorta, while the right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs via the pulmonary artery.

questions.question: Typical 'lub-dub' sounds heard in heart beat are due to;
options: closing of bicuspid and tricuspid valves.
closure of bicuspid and tricuspid valves followed by semilunar valves.
questions.explanation: Explanation:The "Lub-Dub" sounds in a heartbeat are caused by the closure of heart valves in the following sequence: First heart sound ("Lub"): Occurs due to the closure of the atrioventricular (AV) valves (bicuspid/mitral and tricuspid valves) at the beginning of ventricular systole. Second heart sound ("Dub"): Occurs due to the closure of the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonary valves) at the beginning of ventricular diastole. Option A is incorrect because it only mentions AV valves, ignoring semilunar valves. Option B is incorrect because it mentions only semilunar valves, ignoring AV valves. Option C is incorrect because blood pressure in the aorta does not directly cause heart sounds. Thus, the correct answer is D) Closure of bicuspid and tricuspid valves followed by semilunar valves.

hi.question: हृद स्पन्दन में सुनाई देने वाली विशिष्ट 'लब-डब' ध्वनियाँ निम्न के कारण होती हैं;
options: द्विवलनी और त्रिवलनी कपाटों का बंद होना।
महाधमनी के माध्यम से रक्त में दबाव ।
द्विवलनी और त्रिवलनी कपाटों का बंद होना और उसके बाद अर्द्धचंद्राकार कपाटों का बंद होना।
hi.explanation: दिल की धड़कन में "लब-डब" ध्वनियाँ निम्नलिखित क्रम में हृदय वाल्वों के बंद होने के कारण होती हैं:• पहली हृदय ध्वनि ("लब"): निलय प्रकुंचन की शुरुआत में एट्रियोवेंट्रिकुलर (एवी) वाल्व (बाइकस्पिड/माइट्रल और ट्राइकस्पिड वाल्व) के बंद होने के कारण होती है।• दूसरी हृदय ध्वनि ("डब"): निलय डायस्टोल की शुरुआत में अर्धचंद्र वाल्व (महाधमनीय और फुफ्फुसीय वाल्व) के बंद होने के कारण होती है।• विकल्प (A) गलत है क्योंकि इसमें केवल एवी वाल्वों का उल्लेख है, अर्धचंद्र वाल्वों को नजरअंदाज किया गया है।• विकल्प (B) गलत है क्योंकि इसमें केवल अर्धचंद्र वाल्वों का उल्लेख है, एवी वाल्वों को नजरअंदाज किया गया है।• विकल्प (C) गलत है क्योंकि महाधमनी में रक्तचाप सीधे हृदय ध्वनियों का कारण नहीं बनता है।इस प्रकार, सही उत्तर है (D) द्विकपर्दी और त्रिकपर्दी वाल्वों का बंद होना जिसके बाद अर्धचंद्र वाल्वों का बंद होना।

questions.question: How many cardiac cycles are performed per minute?
questions.explanation: A healthy human heart beats 72 times per minute on average. Each heartbeat represents a cardiac cycle, which includes both atrial and ventricular systole and diastole. Therefore, approximately 72 cardiac cycles are performed per minute under normal resting conditions.

questions.question: Which among the following is correct during each cardiac cycle?
options: The volume of blood pumped out by the right and left ventricles is same
The volume of blood pumped out by the right and left ventricles is different
The volume of blood received by each atrium is different
The volume of blood received by the aorta and pulmonary artery is different
questions.explanation: During each cardiac cycle, the right and left ventricles pump out the same volume of blood to maintain continuous and balanced circulation. The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery (pulmonary circulation), while the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta (systemic circulation). This ensures that the amount of blood returning to the heart remains balanced between the two circuits.

questions.question: During ventricular systole
options: Oxygenated blood is pumped into the pulmonary artery and deoxygenated blood is pumped into the artery
Oxygenated blood is pumped into the aorta and deoxygenated blood is pumped into the pulmonary vein
Oxygenated blood is pumped into the pulmonary vein and deoxygenated blood is pumped into the pulmonary artery
Oxygenated blood is pumped into the aorta and deoxygenated blood is pumped into the pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: During ventricular systole, the ventricles contract, forcing blood into the major arteries. The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta, which distributes it to the body (systemic circulation). The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery, which carries it to the lungs for oxygenation (pulmonary circulation). Thus, the correct answer is: Oxygenated blood is pumped into the aorta and deoxygenated blood is pumped into the pulmonary artery.

questions.question: What happens when the pacemaker is non- functional?
options: Only the auricles will contract rhythmically
The cardiac muscles do not contract in a coordinated manner rhythmically
questions.explanation: The pacemaker of the heart (SA node) is responsible for generating electrical impulses that regulate the rhythmic contraction of the heart. If the SA node becomes non-functional, the cardiac muscles do not contract in a coordinated and rhythmic manner, leading to an irregular heartbeat or arrhythmia. This can cause inefficient blood circulation and may require an artificial pacemaker to restore normal heart rhythm.

questions.question: What would be the heart rate of a person if the cardiac output is 5 {~L} , blood volume in the ventricles at the end of the diastole is 100 {~mL} and at the end of ventricular systole is 50 {~mL} ?
questions.explanation: Stroke volume = End Diastolic Volume - End Systolic Volume = 100ml - 50ml = 50ml To achieve cardiac output of 5000ml, No. of Heart beat required = 5000ml/50ml = 100 beats/ min

questions.question: In the ventricular diastole, the ___A_____ valve closes. This causes the second heart sound ____B______ Choose the correct option for A and B
questions.explanation: Explanation: During ventricular diastole, the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonary valves) close to prevent the backflow of blood into the ventricles. This closure of semilunar valves produces the second heart sound ("Dub"). The first heart sound ("Lub") is caused by the closure of the atrioventricular (AV) valves (bicuspid/mitral and tricuspid valves) at the beginning of ventricular systole. Thus, the correct answer is A) A - semilunar, B - dub.

hi.question: निलयी अनुशिथिलन में, A कपाट बंद हो जाता है। इससे द्वितीय हृदय ध्वनि B उत्पन्न होती है।A और B के लिए सही विकल्प चुनिए
hi.explanation: • निलयी डायस्टोल के दौरान, अर्धचंद्र वाल्व (महाधमनीय और फुफ्फुसीय वाल्व) बंद हो जाते हैं ताकि निलयों में रक्त का पश्चप्रवाह न हो।• अर्धचंद्र वाल्वों के इस बंद होने से दूसरी हृदय ध्वनि ("डब") उत्पन्न होती है।• पहली हृदय ध्वनि ("लब") निलयी सिस्टोल की शुरुआत में एट्रियोवेंट्रिकुलर (एवी) वाल्व (बाइकस्पिड/माइट्रल और ट्राइकस्पिड वाल्व) के बंद होने के कारण होती है।इस प्रकार, सही उत्तर है (A)

questions.question: Determination of the cardiac output is done by
questions.explanation: Cardiac output (CO) is determined by the heart rate (HR) and stroke volume (SV). It is calculated using the formula: Cardiac Output=Stroke Volume×Heart Rate{Cardiac Output} = {Stroke Volume} {Heart Rate} Where: Heart rate (HR) = Number of heartbeats per minute (~72 bpm in a healthy adult). Stroke volume (SV) = Amount of blood pumped by each ventricle per beat (~70 mL). Normal cardiac output = 5-6 liters per minute in an average adult.

questions.question: Cardiac output is:
options: Volume of the blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute
Volume of the blood contained in the entire heart
Volume of the oxygenated blood pumped by heart
Volume of the deoxygenated blood pumped by heart
questions.explanation: Cardiac output (CO) refers to the total volume of blood pumped by each ventricle per minute. It is calculated using the formula: Cardiac Output=Stroke Volume×Heart Rate{Cardiac Output} = {Stroke Volume} {Heart Rate} Where: Stroke volume (SV) = Amount of blood pumped per beat (~70 mL). Heart rate (HR) = Beats per minute (~72 bpm). Normal cardiac output = 5-6 liters per minute in a healthy adult. Option B is incorrect because CO refers to blood pumped per minute, not the total volume in the heart. Option C and D are incorrect because CO includes both oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, depending on which ventricle is being considered.

questions.question: Choose the incorrect pair
options: Lub Sharp closure of AV valve
questions.explanation: Explanation: Option A is incorrect: The second heart sound ("Dub") is produced due to the closure (not opening) of the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonary valves) at the beginning of ventricular diastole. Option B is correct: The first heart sound ("Lub") is caused by the sharp closure of atrioventricular (AV) valves (tricuspid and bicuspid/mitral valves) at the beginning of ventricular systole. Option C is correct: The Sinoatrial (SA) node is the natural pacemaker of the heart and initiates the heartbeat. Option D is correct: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs for oxygenation. Thus, the incorrect pair is A) Dub → Opening of semilunar valve.

hi.question: गलत युग्म का चयन कीजिए
options: लब → एवी कपाट का तेजी से बंद होना
हृदय स्पंदन का प्रारंभ → एसए नोड
hi.explanation: • विकल्प (A) गलत है: दूसरी हृदय ध्वनि ("डब") निलयी डायस्टोल की शुरुआत में अर्धचंद्र वाल्व (महाधमनीय और फुफ्फुसीय वाल्व) के बंद होने (खुलने नहीं) के कारण उत्पन्न होती है।• विकल्प (B) सही है: पहली हृदय ध्वनि ("लब") निलयी सिस्टोल की शुरुआत में एट्रियोवेंट्रिकुलर (एवी) वाल्व (ट्राइकस्पिड और बाइकस्पिड/माइट्रल वाल्व) के तेजी से बंद होने के कारण होती है।• विकल्प (C) सही है: साइनोएट्रियल (एसए) नोड हृदय का प्राकृतिक पेसमेकर है और हृदय की धड़कन शुरू करता है।• विकल्प (D) सही है: फुफ्फुसीय धमनी दाएं निलय से फेफड़ों तक ऑक्सीजन रहित रक्त ले जाती है ताकि ऑक्सीजनकरण हो सके।इस प्रकार, गलत जोड़ी है (A) डब → अर्धचंद्र वाल्व का खुलना।

questions.question: The second heart sound (dub) is associated with the closure of:
questions.explanation: The second heart sound ("dub") occurs due to the closure of the semilunar valves at the beginning of ventricular diastole. The semilunar valves include: Pulmonary valve (prevents backflow from the pulmonary artery into the right ventricle). Aortic valve (prevents backflow from the aorta into the left ventricle). When the ventricles relax after contraction, the pressure in the arteries becomes higher than in the ventricles, causing the semilunar valves to close, producing the "dub" sound.

questions.question: What would be the cardiac output of a person having 72 heart beats per minute and a stroke volume of 50 {~mL} ?
questions.explanation: Cardiac output (CO) is calculated using the formula: Cardiac Output=Stroke Volume×Heart Rate{Cardiac Output} = {Stroke Volume} {Heart Rate} Given: Heart rate (HR) = 72 beats per minute Stroke volume (SV) = 50 mL per beat CO=72×50CO = 72 50 CO=3600 mL/min (or 3.6 L/min)CO = 3600 { mL/min} { (or 3.6 L/min)}

questions.question: An adult human with average health has systolic and diastolic pressures as
questions.explanation: In a healthy adult human, the normal blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, where: 120 mmHg represents the systolic pressure (pressure during ventricular contraction). 80 mmHg represents the diastolic pressure (pressure during ventricular relaxation). This standard value ensures proper circulation and oxygen delivery to body tissues.

questions.question: Blood pressure in the mammalian aorta is maximum during
questions.explanation: Blood pressure in the mammalian aorta is maximum during the systole (contraction) of the left ventricle. This is because the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood with high pressure into the aorta, which distributes it to the entire body (systemic circulation). During ventricular systole, the forceful contraction of the left ventricle generates the highest blood pressure (systolic pressure, typically 120 mmHg in a healthy adult).

questions.question: Which one of the following statement is correct regarding blood pressure?
options: 190 / 110 {~mm} {Hg} may harm vital organs like brain and kidney
140 / 90 {~mm} {Hg} is considered high and requires treatment
100 / 55 {~mm} {Hg} is considered an ideal blood pressure
questions.explanation: A blood pressure of 190/110 mmHg is severely high (hypertension) and can damage vital organs such as the brain, kidneys, and heart. Uncontrolled hypertension increases the risk of stroke, heart failure, kidney damage, and aneurysms. 140/90 mmHg is considered mild hypertension and may require treatment depending on the individual's health condition. 100/55 mmHg is on the lower side and may not be ideal for all individuals. 105/50 mmHg does not necessarily make one more active; it may lead to symptoms like dizziness and fatigue in some cases.

questions.question: Which of the following nerves inhibit the rate of heart beat?
questions.explanation: The vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) is part of the parasympathetic nervous system and plays a crucial role in reducing the heart rate. It releases acetylcholine, which slows down the sinoatrial (SA) node activity, thereby inhibiting the rate of the heartbeat. Sympathetic nerves (Option B) do the opposite; they increase heart rate by releasing noradrenaline. Oculomotor nerve (Option C) controls eye movement and has no role in heart regulation.

questions.question: Atrial diastole takes place when
options: Right atrium is filled with blood
Left atrium is filled with blood
Both atriums are filled with blood
Both ventricles are filled with blood
questions.explanation: Atrial diastole is the relaxation phase of both atria, allowing them to fill with blood from the vena cava (right atrium) and pulmonary veins (left atrium). During atrial diastole, both atria are relaxed, and blood flows in passively from the veins. This occurs while the ventricles are in systole (contracting), pumping blood into the pulmonary artery and aorta. Once the atria are filled, atrial systole follows, pushing blood into the ventricles.

questions.question: Which wave of human heart out of PQRST, is used for determining the heartbeat of an individual?
questions.explanation: The QRS complex in an ECG represents the depolarization of the ventricles, which initiates ventricular contraction (systole). Since the heartbeat is determined by the rhythmic contraction of the ventricles, the number of QRS complexes per minute is used to calculate the heart rate of an individual.

questions.question: Blood circulation that starts in capillaries and ends in capillaries is called:
questions.explanation: Portal circulation is a type of blood circulation that begins in one capillary network and ends in another capillary network without passing through the heart first. Example: Hepatic portal circulation, where blood from the intestinal capillaries flows through the hepatic portal vein to the liver capillaries before entering systemic circulation. Other options: Hepatic circulation (B) → Refers to blood flow in the liver, but not specifically capillary-to-capillary circulation. Lymphatic circulation (C) → Involves lymph movement, not blood circulation. Renal circulation (D) → Refers to kidney blood flow, but does not involve capillary-to-capillary transfer. Thus, the correct answer is A (Portal circulation).

questions.question: Statement-I: Each cardiac cycle consists of systole and diastole of both the atria and ventricles. Statement-II: The cardiac output of an ordinary man will be much higher than that of an athlete.
options: Statement I and Statement II both are correct.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
Statement I and Statement II both are incorrect.
questions.explanation: Explanation: Statement I is correct: A cardiac cycle consists of systole (contraction) and diastole (relaxation) of both the atria and ventricles. This ensures efficient blood circulation throughout the body. Statement II is incorrect: Athletes have a higher cardiac output (CO) than ordinary individuals, not lower. Cardiac output = Stroke volume × Heart rate Athletes have a higher stroke volume (due to stronger heart muscles) and a lower resting heart rate, leading to greater efficiency in pumping blood. In contrast, an ordinary individual has a higher resting heart rate but a lower stroke volume, resulting in a lower overall cardiac output compared to an athlete. This follows NCERT Biology, which explains how regular exercise enhances cardiac efficiency, increasing stroke volume while reducing heart rate.

hi.question: कथन-I: प्रत्येक हृद चक्र में आलिंद और निलय दोनों का प्रकुंचन और अनुशिथिलन होता है।कथन-II: एक साधारण मनुष्य का हृद निकास एक एथलीट की तुलना में बहुत अधिक होगा।
options: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।
कथन I सही है, लेकिन कथन II गलत है।
कथन I गलत है, लेकिन कथन II सही है।
कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।
hi.explanation: • कथन I सही है:• एक हृदय चक्र में अलिंद और निलय दोनों का सिस्टोल (संकुचन) और डायस्टोल (विश्राम) होता है।• यह पूरे शरीर में कुशल रक्त परिसंचरण सुनिश्चित करता है।• कथन II गलत है:• एथलीटों का कार्डियक आउटपुट (CO) सामान्य व्यक्तियों की तुलना में अधिक होता है, कम नहीं।• कार्डियक आउटपुट = स्ट्रोक वॉल्यूम × हृदय गति• एथलीटों का स्ट्रोक वॉल्यूम अधिक होता है (मजबूत हृदय की मांसपेशियों के कारण) और आराम की हृदय गति कम होती है, जिससे रक्त पंप करने में अधिक दक्षता होती है।• इसके विपरीत, एक सामान्य व्यक्ति की आराम की हृदय गति अधिक होती है लेकिन स्ट्रोक वॉल्यूम कम होता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप एथलीट की तुलना में समग्र कार्डियक आउटपुट कम होता है।यह एनसीईआरटी जीवविज्ञान का अनुसरण करता है, जो बताता है कि नियमित व्यायाम हृदय की दक्षता को कैसे बढ़ाता है, स्ट्रोक वॉल्यूम बढ़ाता है जबकि हृदय गति को कम करता है।
